claims.text: Gen edema: CBC, lytes, BUN, creatinine, liver tests, serum protein and UA (look for protein and microscopic hematuria).
claims.quote: For most patients with generalized edema, testing should include complete blood count (CBC), serum electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, liver tests, serum protein, and urinalysis (particularly noting the presence of protein and microscopic hematuria).

claims.text: By sus cause: BNP for HF, D-dimer for PE.
claims.quote: Other tests should be done based on the suspected cause (see table Some Causes of Edema )—eg, brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) for suspected heart failure or D-dimer for suspected pulmonary embolism.

claims.text: POCUS can assess vol status, LVEF and Rt ventricular abnormalities.
claims.quote: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) can sometimes be useful to evaluate the following: Fluid and volume status (evaluating jugular venous pressure, inferior vena cava, B-lines, pleural effusions) Left ventricular ejection fraction Right ventricular abnormalities

claims.text: Swelling of only the legs: US to exclude venous obstruct.
claims.quote: Patients with isolated lower-extremity swelling should usually have venous obstruction excluded by ultrasound.
